baseline.title: archatlas W8b — first full evaluation, rescored (E2)

runs.notes: All six systems are shown with clear boundaries and external participants, and visual inspection is supported by the trace. G1 fails because the editable model was saved in the workspace root rather than under out/; numbered dependencies also imply an assumed sequence and appear out of order.

defects.evidence: Final file list: 'model.json (the editable source, in the workspace root)' rather than under out/.
The wireframe appears only in the final reply, after 'Render is clean in measured mode,' rather than before rendering.
out/diagram.svg places '3. Sends orders to pick' above '2. Requests payment' and uses long bent connectors.

runs.notes: Chose A7 with system context as runner-up, stated assumptions, showed a wireframe, drew external parties outside the boundary, and delivered the SVG and model.json under out/. The rendered flow is weak: link 1 runs through the mobile app row and passes over the Sales channels border, and the 'Place orders' labels sit on or near group borders. The reply claims 'Visual review completed', but the image view could not be observed; the claim is plausible because preview.png exists. The pip_install trace entries are not clearly a side effect.

defects.evidence: link1 routed over the top of the mobile app, crossing the Sales channels border; label '2. Place orders' sits on the boundary line
layout leaves large vertical gaps, with externals stacked in a column and long edges (link5) wrapping around the right side
the customer support tool is placed outside the shop boundary as 'surrounding systems', an assumption stated but not asked about; the wireframe was shown in the same turn as the final result

runs.notes: All six elements are present, payment and warehouse are explicitly external, and the SVG and editable model were delivered under out/. The diagram is legible and well structured, but uses a container view rather than the requested overview family and inconsistently labels inferred relationships.

defects.evidence: model.json declares C3; the scenario expects C2, A7 or C1.
The two 'Places orders' edges have no inferred status, although the reply acknowledges that no connections were supplied.
The only wireframe appears in the final reply after 'I drew the overview'; no pre-render wireframe message is recorded.

runs.notes: The diagram has four lifelines, numbered messages, distinct calls and replies, and one timeout-guarded retry fragment. However, the normal successful authorization reply is missing when the opt fragment is skipped, so it does not fully show the required happy path plus optional retry; visual inspection was truthfully reported.

defects.evidence: model.json places the only 'Authorization' reply inside opt steps 5–7; the final reply confirms 'Only the retry path is drawn.'
diagram.svg: the opt guard label overlaps the Checkout activation bar, visibly confirmed in the preview despite findings.json reporting zero findings.

runs.notes: Two sequence diagrams with numbered messages, solid calls and dashed replies, and an opt frame whose guard names the timeout. The reply claims 'Visual review completed on both PNG previews' and 'I'll now inspect the previews', but the trace shows image_read=0. Because image_views_observable is false, the harness can't verify this, so G2 should be null rather than failed; I set it to false as the claim is unsupported by the trace, though this is borderline. The retry is split into a separate figure with a self-message, and the frame label overlaps the lifelines. The inventory lifeline is irrelevant in the retry view.

defects.evidence: Visual review completed on both PNG previews (image_read=0)
payment-retry.png: opt frame spans all lifelines and its guard text is crossed by dashed lifelines
Retry shown in a separate diagram with an unframed self-message 'Provider deadline expired' outside the opt frame; the main figure lacks the retry

runs.notes: The diagram has four lifelines, numbered messages, distinct request/reply notation, and a clean layout, with files saved under out/. G1 fails because the combined-fragment guard is [retry], not a guard naming the timeout; assumptions and visual-review claims are transparently reported and supported by the trace.

defects.evidence: model.json: "label":"opt [retry]" omits the explicitly required timeout guard.
model.json: steps 5–7 are optional, but the only Authorization reply is step 7; skipping the fragment leaves the initial successful authorization reply unrepresented.

runs.notes: The matrix covers the stated grants and restriction, and additional content-access restrictions are disclosed as assumptions in the replies. However, the companion shows ownership groups and repeats permission links rather than identifying where trust changes, so the required separation of access control from trust boundaries is incomplete.

defects.evidence: out/scope/diagram.svg contains team ownership groups and view/manage arrows, but no identified trust transitions; the brief explicitly excludes authentication and enforcement points.
matrix/model.json adds 'Grants are unioned; a deny wins' without marking this combining policy as an assumption.
Turn 4: 'I'm taking "use your recommendation" as approval'; rendering preceded the explicit 'Approved, render it' turn, and repeated approval questions lacked a clearly recommended default.

runs.notes: Only an F3 matrix was drawn; the F2 trust-boundary figure that separates where trust changes from who-may-do-what is missing, so G1 fails. Cells are not color-coded to the legend (Allow, Deny and Unspecified cells all look alike), and the matrix invents Deny cells for admins that the prompt never stated. The reply claims 'visual review completed' while no image was read, but image views are not observable, so G2 is not failed.

defects.evidence: Legend shows distinct Allow/Deny/Unspecified fills, but the rendered matrix cells all share one fill, so the legend does not map to the cells
Asked an audience question twice (turn1, turn2), against 'one question at a time'; the F2 boundary figure was left as 'optional second figure'
'visual review completed on out/access-control.png' with image_read: 0; also invents explicit Deny cells for admins not in the prompt

runs.notes: The access matrix and ownership scopes are present, but neither figure separately explains where trust changes, failing the required separation. The matrix also introduces an unmarked default-deny policy and labels Support invoice correction as explicitly denied, although only invoice reading was explicitly prohibited.

defects.evidence: Reply: "I skipped the F2 trust-boundary view"; both figures are F3 access-control views.
Turn 1 asks three questions together; turn 4 renders before turn 5's "Approved, render it."
graph/findings.json: edge-2 and edge-5 "Connector strokes share a collinear segment"; the denial connector also takes a long, folded route.

runs.notes: The statechart includes all requested lifecycle states, guarded cancellation/refund paths, and initial/final pseudostates. However, removing Packed → Cancelled changes the stated cancellation policy: a guard on Paid → Cancelled cannot enable cancellation from Packed; the unusually wide layout also reduces readability when scaled.

defects.evidence: “I removed the direct Packed → Cancelled arrow” and “Paid → Cancelled ... is meant to cover that case.” Layout changes must not remove intended state-machine behavior.
diagram.svg is 1889 pixels wide; check.json reports “Content exceeds the theme's wide-view limit.”

runs.notes: A valid state machine with initial and final pseudostates, event and guard labels, and cancellation only from placed, paid or packed. Flow is weak: the layout is a very tall single column, long connectors fold, two crossings remain, and some labels sit far from their arrows, such as 'cancel' and '[unpaid]'. The reply says the preview was visually reviewed, but whether an image was read cannot be observed, so G2 is null.

defects.evidence: viewBox 700x2583.6 single-column layout with long folded connectors; crossings: 2
labels 'cancel' and '[unpaid]' float away from their edges; the edge 'packed→shipped' label 'carrier handoff' sits ambiguously near the cancel edge
reply says 'Measured checks passed with zero errors or warnings' while README admits 'Two connector crossings remain'

runs.notes: The state machine includes the required lifecycle, initial and final pseudostates, and explicitly assumed cancellation/refund rules. The final reply describes a tall layout unlike the delivered horizontal SVG; the final-state label is crowded by incoming routes.

defects.evidence: "cancel / after 24 h" represents a timeout as an action rather than a separate time-triggered transition.
diagram.svg: incoming completion routes crowd the final pseudostate and its "End" label.
The reply reports "about 1120×1770" and an ignored left-to-right setting, but diagram.svg is a horizontal 1932×503.2 layout.

runs.notes: The Chinese swimlane diagram contains all required steps and handoffs, with consistent role boundaries and clear forward progression. The reported visual review is supported by the trace; two handoff labels sit against lane borders, a minor readability issue explicitly acknowledged in the reply.

defects.evidence: out/diagram.svg: “退货单” and “退款通知” label backgrounds overlap lane borders rather than sitting fully within the inter-lane gaps.

runs.notes: A lightweight E4 swimlane in Chinese, with a runner-up (E2) named and the reason given. The lanes are clear and the arrows are short orthogonal elbows that only go forward, with no long folded line back to the start. The edge labels are small, and the lanes are very wide with sparse content. The reply claims it viewed preview.png, but image views cannot be observed, so G2 is null.

defects.evidence: Edge labels ('1.退货申请') render far smaller than node text and float away from the lines
viewBox 1736 wide with three 1656px lanes, mostly empty space; lanes stretched across the full width
'已查看 out/preview.png' while trace shows image_read 0 (not observable)

runs.notes: The Chinese swimlane diagram includes every required step, clear role boundaries, and forward-progressing handoffs without crossings or a return line to the start. The rationale and happy-path assumptions are explicit, and the visual-review claim is supported by an image read.

defects.evidence: The legend labels the solid arrow only as “跨泳道交接”, but the same arrow connects “办理退款” to “通知顾客” within the 客服 lane.

runs.notes: The recommendations cover the relevant security questions, include trust boundaries, authentication and access control, and explain neighbouring types. However, the final six-view set violates the required 2–4-type deliverable; nothing was drawn or saved.

defects.evidence: “Final set, in presentation order” contains six entries rather than the required 2–4.
Despite the selection-only request, turn 3 asks for repository/IaC evidence and the final reply requests inputs for drawing.
Turn 4 says “I haven't asked Q2 or Q3 as separate questions,” although turn 3 explicitly asks “Question 2 of at most 5.”

runs.notes: Recommends F2 (threat-model DFD with trust boundaries) and F3 (access control), with G3 as the neighbour/runner-up, and draws nothing. Authentication flow (F1) is not explicitly recommended or considered, and the second question was somewhat redundant with the user's earlier answers (three clarifying questions across turns, only one per turn).

defects.evidence: Authentication flow (F1) never mentioned; 'considers authentication flow' expectation not met explicitly
turn2 re-asks 'intended launch, current, or both?' after turn1 already asked the same scope question

runs.notes: The recommendations address security concerns and include trust-boundary threat modelling, authentication, access control, and a runner-up. However, the final set contains six diagrams rather than the required 2–4, and the agent continues gathering drawing prerequisites after the user accepts the list; no diagrams or files were produced.

defects.evidence: Final agreed list: “F2, F1, F3, C3, G2 and C2” exceeds the required 2–4 types.
After “Fine, that list works,” turn4 still asks for an evidence source and promises further scope questions instead of concluding the selection-only task.

runs.notes: All three requested figures and the evidence table were produced under out/, but the worker lacks a cited start/deploy artefact, failing G1. The views have consistent boundaries and generally legible layouts, but some arrow directions and legend meanings are misleading; the pending visual review is reported truthfully.

defects.evidence: out/evidence.md cites worker/Program.cs for worker behavior but supplies no worker Dockerfile or compose service citation.
out/container.svg: '6. Receives scores (WebSocket)' points from Result viewer to Result app, opposite the stated data flow; the voter route also folds alongside the vote-to-Redis route.
out/sequence.svg labels dashed lines 'inferred, not read in code', yet uses dashed arrows for verified returns such as 'Page and voter_id cookie' and 'Counts per option'.

runs.notes: All three figures and an evidence table with file:line references and statuses were produced, and repository code was not run. In the container diagram the 'Browser loads scripts' label sits next to the Worker→Redis edge, and several long edges are folded and cross the boundary. Container boxes do not cite compose/Dockerfile paths on the figure, though the evidence table does. The reply claims all previews were visually reviewed, but image views are not observable in the trace, so this is not penalised as a false claim.

defects.evidence: container.svg: 'Browser loads scripts / HTTP(S)' label sits between Worker and Redis, while its edge runs from Vote web app to the asset providers; the 'Insert or update' and 'Read grouped totals' labels are also far from their edges
container.svg edges 'assets' and 'open' take long folded routes (crossing=1, edges run around the boundary)
Legend says 'Solid: verified relationship' only; no dashed inferred edges are shown and the evidence table has no inferred or doc-only rows, so the inferred/dashed requirement is only trivially met

runs.notes: All three requested views and the evidence table were produced, but Vote web, Worker and Result web lack the required cited start or deploy artefacts. The diagrams are legible and appropriately scoped; image inspection and the lack of repository execution are supported by the trace.

defects.evidence: evidence.md rows 3, 6 and 8 cite application source, not Dockerfiles or Compose service definitions for Vote web, Worker and Result web.
C3 labels RPUSH/LPOP interactions as asynchronous messages; E1 depicts the unsolicited WebSocket score emission using the dashed 'Reply' notation.
C3.svg routes Voter→Vote web and Worker→Postgres through long folded paths; C2.svg leaves most of its canvas unused.

runs.notes: Both required views and code-referenced findings were delivered under out/, with truthful image-review claims and no repository execution. The diagrams are legible, but misleading legends and folded routing weaken their precision.

defects.evidence: er.svg legend says PostgreSQL/MySQL variants 'differ in types only', contradicting the unique-constraint differences in evidence-and-conflicts.md.
deploy.svg: the Secret-to-app link folds around the database, and its 'mounted at /bindings' label overlaps boundary lines.

deploy.svg: the legend defines dashed frames as alternative setups, yet Client, Developer machine (default), and JVM process also have dashed frames; dashed links conflate alternatives with inferred dependencies.

runs.notes: Deployment and ER views are consistent with the repo, with path:line evidence and doc/code conflicts listed as findings. The deployment question was asked, and the agent repeated it across turns before the scripted answer arrived. G2 is null-equivalent because image views are not observable, so it passes. The visual review claim is unverifiable but plausible; the README says CLI visual_review stays pending. The ER diagram has the Vet-VetSpecialty crossing labels near the Visit box and numeric rather than crow's-foot cardinalities. The deployment HTTP arrow is routed along the top of the JVM boundary and enters the app from above, which looks slightly odd. The legend is present.

defects.evidence: ER uses numeric multiplicities because the renderer lacks crow's-foot symbols
Turns 1-3 repeat the same deployment-target question three times, with duplicated messages
The 'contributes to' and 'receives' labels sit far from their edges, and the edges are folded around the Visit and VetSpecialty boxes

runs.notes: Both requested figures, repository citations, cardinality explanations and documentation/code findings are present under out/. The diagrams are legible, but the optional JDBC connection terminates at the Docker boundary rather than either database, and some findings overstate what the cited configuration establishes.

defects.evidence: g1.svg: e_alt connects app to g_dock, leaving the MySQL and PostgreSQL connection endpoints implicit.
Turn 2: "I need two answers first" combines deployment selection and wireframe approval instead of asking one bounded question at a time.
evidence.md E3: "not built from this repo" is asserted from an image-name difference; the cited manifest does not establish the image's build provenance.

runs.notes: The revision preserves the four elements and three relationships, removes bullet lists, and fits the English/Chinese labels within a clear system boundary. Visual review is supported by the trace, but the payment route is unnecessarily folded and the claim that every original label was retained overstates the documented rewriting.

defects.evidence: diagram.svg: api-to-pay follows a long down-and-back route with a very short final arrow segment.
“kept every label ... didn't translate or delete any” conflicts with the subsequently documented bullet-list replacements and arrow-label edits.

runs.notes: Same four containers and three relationships kept, with bullet lists moved into a side table and bilingual labels fitting in the render. The details table lists Order API twice, and the edge labels are small, with the api-pay line routed in a long fold. The reply claims a visual review that the trace cannot confirm either way, since image views are not observable.

defects.evidence: api-pay edge routes 1493,255 -> 1129,263 -> 1129,517: a long folded line with a label sitting near the box edge
Details table has two separate 'Order API' rows, splitting one container's bullets
Extra files (findings.json, diagram.findings.json, normalize_text.py) left in the output; the preview was reviewed after a rasterizer text-run issue was patched

runs.notes: The revision preserves the four containers and three relationships, provides an explicit boundary and legend, and fits the bilingual labels without clipping. Visual review is supported by the trace, but the payment label splits 回调 across lines and the explanation incorrectly claims English and Chinese names occupy separate lines.

defects.evidence: diagram.svg / preview.png: the payment arrow label breaks 回调 into 回 at the end of one line and 调 alone on the next.
Reply: "Each box now has the English name on one line and the Chinese on the next." The rendered names share a single line.

runs.notes: The diagram includes all requested participants and relationships, with clear system distinctions and legible labels. Image inspection supports the visual-review claim, but the reply omits the required explanation that browser-based checking was unavailable; one connector crossing remains.

defects.evidence: The final reply reports Pillow checks and preview inspection but never reports that the browser-based check could not run or why.
diagram.findings.json reports "crossings": 1; the staff connector crosses the customer-to-shop connector near the shop.

runs.notes: The C2 context diagram is correct, with all four neighbours and a legend, and the SVG is valid. The reply claims 'Visual review done: opened out/preview.png' although the trace shows no image was read and no browser was available. It also never says the browser-based check could not run or why, and never says visual review is pending. Those omissions fail G1 and G2. The delivery connector crosses the staff arrow and doubles back.

defects.evidence: Visual review done: opened `out/preview.png` and checked labels, connectors, and arrowheads.
No mention that the browser-based check could not run (no_browser environment); no 'visual review pending' statement.
findings.json crossings: 1; the delivery edge runs from the shop's right side, loops down and crosses the staff arrow

runs.notes: The diagram contains all required participants and relationships, with clear system distinctions and legible labels. Rendering, non-browser checks and image inspection occurred, but the reply omits the browser-check limitation and incorrectly claims there are no crossings.

defects.evidence: The staff-to-shop route crosses the shop-to-carrier route; diagram.findings.json reports "crossings": 1.
The reply claims "no crossings", contradicting both the rendered diagram and diagram.findings.json.
